# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the old billing system to the new one while both systems run in parallel (dual-run). Migration proceeds in named phases, each gated by an entry criterion and monitored against halt thresholds. The old billing system remains fully operational (not disabled or decommissioned) throughout all user-migration phases, including the final one; decommissioning is explicitly deferred to a separate, later phase after the last batch of users has been migrated and validated.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2.5% of users — 1,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging (including invoicing, payment capture, refunds, and proration), dual-write/dual-read reconciliation tooling is live, and an internal rollback procedure has been rehearsed at least once in staging.

**Scope:** 1,000 users selected from internal/employee accounts and consenting low-risk external customers (e.g., accounts with no active disputes, non-enterprise contracts).

**Activities:**
- Migrate accounts to the new system while keeping old system as system-of-record fallback.
- Run parallel billing cycles on both systems and reconcile invoice totals, tax calculations, and payment statuses daily.
- Collect support ticket volume and reconciliation discrepancies.

**Exit criterion to advance:** ≤0.5% invoice mismatch rate between systems over 2 consecutive billing cycles, and no critical (Sev-1) incidents open.

---

## Phase 2: Expanded Rollout (25% of users — 10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met, reconciliation discrepancy rate stayed below threshold for 2 consecutive billing cycles, and support ticket volume attributable to migration is below 1% of migrated users.

**Scope:** Broader mix of customer segments (varied plan types, geographies, payment methods) but excluding highest-revenue enterprise accounts.

**Activities:**
- Batch migration in waves of ~2,000 users every 3–5 days, with reconciliation checks between waves.
- Enable customer-facing communication (billing statement notices) explaining the transition.
- Load-test new system under real concurrent billing volume.

**Exit criterion to advance:** Payment failure rate on migrated accounts stays within 0.2 percentage points of the old system's baseline failure rate, and reconciliation mismatch rate remains ≤0.5%.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability / Full Migration (72.5% of users — 29,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met, finance sign-off obtained on reconciliation accuracy, and customer support has confirmed staffing/readiness for full-volume ticket load.

**Scope:** All remaining users, including enterprise and highest-revenue accounts, migrated last due to contract complexity.

**Activities:**
- Migrate remaining users in waves (e.g., 5,000–7,000 per wave) with a 48–72 hour monitoring window between waves.
- Enterprise accounts migrated individually with dedicated account-manager coordination.
- Both systems continue running in parallel through the end of this phase; the old system remains fully operational as fallback for every migrated user until post-migration validation is complete.

**Exit criterion (phase complete, not a decommission trigger):** 100% of users migrated, reconciliation mismatch rate ≤0.5% sustained for 2 full billing cycles across the entire user base, and zero unresolved Sev-1 billing incidents.

---

## Phase 4: Legacy Decommission (0% of users — infrastructure only, no user migration activity)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete, a minimum 2 full billing cycles have elapsed post-final-migration with no reconciliation discrepancies above threshold, and finance/compliance have signed off that no regulatory retention requirement blocks legacy shutdown.

**Activities:** Archive legacy billing data per retention policy, disable dual-write, decommission old billing system infrastructure.

*(This phase is intentionally separated from Phase 3 so that decommissioning the old system never occurs in the same phase as the final batch of user migration.)*

---

## Risks

RISK: Reconciliation mismatches between old and new systems cause incorrect customer charges | Run automated daily reconciliation with alerting; require manual sign-off before advancing any phase | Finance Systems Lead
RISK: Payment gateway integration behaves differently under new system, causing elevated payment failures | Load-test gateway integration in staging with production-like traffic; monitor failure rate in real time during rollout | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Migrated enterprise customers experience billing disruption affecting contractual SLAs | Migrate enterprise accounts last, individually, with dedicated account-manager coordination and rollback plan per account | Enterprise Customer Success Lead
RISK: Support team is overwhelmed by ticket volume during rollout, delaying issue resolution | Stagger wave sizes, forecast ticket volume from pilot data, and pre-scale support staffing before each phase | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Data corruption or loss during account migration between systems | Use idempotent migration scripts with pre/post checksums on account and invoice data; keep old system as read fallback until validated | Data Migration Engineering Lead

---

## Halt Criteria (Automatic Rollout Pause)

The rollout must pause immediately and roll back the current wave if any of the following occur:
- **Reconciliation mismatch rate exceeds 1.0%** of migrated accounts in any single billing cycle.
- **Payment failure rate on migrated accounts exceeds baseline (old-system) failure rate by more than 0.5 percentage points** in any 24-hour window.
- Any Sev-1 billing incident (e.g., duplicate charges, failed refunds at scale) remains unresolved for more than 4 hours.

---

## Notes on Numeric Consistency

- 2.5% of 40,000 = 1,000 ✓
- 25% of 40,000 = 10,000 ✓
- 72.5% of 40,000 = 29,000 ✓
- 1,000 + 10,000 + 29,000 = 40,000 ✓ (100% of users accounted for across the three user-migration phases)
- Phase 4 carries 0% user-migration share by design, since it is infrastructure decommissioning only, occurring strictly after Phase 3's final batch.

PHASES: 4
